[Feature][Op][MRV2] Optimize gumbel_sample with hierarchical categorical sampling on NPU (#16269)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR optimizes `gumbel_sample` for MRV2 on Ascend NPU by replacing
the original vocabulary-wide Gumbel-Max path with a
distribution-equivalent Triton `categorical_sample` implementation.

The original Gumbel-Max implementation generates one random value for
every vocabulary element, applies the Gumbel transform, and then
performs `argmax`:

```text
logits
  -> optional temperature scaling
  -> U_i ~ Uniform(0, 1) for every vocab element
  -> g_i = -log(-log(U_i))
  -> logits + g_i
  -> argmax
```

For large vocabularies such as `V=151936`, this is expensive on NPU
because the random-number generation and transcendental operations scale
with `B × V`.

For non-zero temperature, Gumbel-Max is distribution-equivalent to
directly sampling from the categorical distribution defined by
`softmax(logits / T)`. This PR therefore changes the implementation
strategy while preserving the sampling probability distribution.

The optimized path uses a two-stage hierarchical categorical sampler:

```text
8192-element coarse block
        ↓
prepare block max / argmax / probability mass
        ↓
prepare 8 × 1024 fine-block masses
        ↓
sample one coarse block
        ↓
sample one 1024-element fine block
        ↓
reload only the selected 1024 logits
        ↓
final cumulative-mass search
        ↓
sampled token
```

The main implementation details are:

- Split each vocabulary row into **8192-element coarse blocks**.
- `_categorical_prepare_mass_kernel` computes:
  - block max / argmax,
  - coarse-block probability mass,
  - **8 × 1024 fine-block masses** for each coarse block.
- `_categorical_sample_kernel`:
  - samples one coarse block,
  - samples one prepared 1024-element fine block,
- reloads only the selected 1024 logits for the final cumulative-mass
search.
- Only **one stateless uniform random draw per sampled row** is required
instead of one random value per vocabulary element.
- `(token, coarse_block)` prepare tasks and token sampling tasks are
distributed according to the available Vector Core count.
- Draft sampling uses a separate stateless RNG namespace by adding `1 <<
30` to the random position.
- Pre-imported sampler/speculator modules are explicitly rebound to
`categorical_sample`, because those modules may be imported before the
Ascend patch is applied.

The existing sampling contract is preserved:

- `temperature == 0`: greedy `argmax`.
- `temperature != 0`: categorical sampling from the same probability
distribution as Gumbel-Max.
- `apply_temperature` behavior is preserved.
- `expanded_idx_mapping`, `seed`, `pos`, `logits_cache`, and
`logits_cache_col` behavior is preserved.
- Raw logits are written to `logits_cache` before temperature scaling.
- CUDAGraph padding rows with request index `-1` do not write the cache.
- `use_fp64=True` remains unsupported on NPU and raises
`NotImplementedError`.

This work follows the direct-categorical-sampling direction explored in
#16176, while using an NPU-specific hierarchical 8K/1K implementation to
reduce the final scan size and avoid vocabulary-wide random-number
generation.

---

### Performance

Performance was measured with `msprof op`. The categorical operator is
profiled as two Triton kernels:

```text
categorical total
=
_categorical_prepare_mass_kernel
+
_categorical_sample_kernel
```

The numbers below are kernel `Task Duration(us)` and do not include
Python wrapper or synchronized host-side wall time.

#### Categorical scaling on A3, FP32, `temperature=1`

Batch growth with `V=151936`:

| Batch | Vocab | Prepare Mass | Sample | Total |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 151936 | 7.08 us | 25.78 us | **32.86 us** |
| 16 | 151936 | 34.34 us | 24.20 us | **58.54 us** |
| 32 | 151936 | 62.40 us | 25.28 us | **87.68 us** |
| 64 | 151936 | 117.48 us | 46.56 us | **164.04 us** |
| 128 | 151936 | 227.44 us | 88.10 us | **315.54 us** |
| 256 | 151936 | 448.78 us | 150.22 us | **599.00 us** |
| 512 | 151936 | 889.58 us | 273.84 us | **1163.42 us** |

Vocabulary scaling with `B=64`:

| Batch | Vocab | Prepare Mass | Sample | Total |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 32768 | 30.42 us | 45.76 us | **76.18 us** |
| 64 | 65536 | 51.84 us | 45.88 us | **97.72 us** |
| 64 | 131072 | 99.02 us | 45.58 us | **144.60 us** |
| 64 | 151936 | 117.48 us | 46.56 us | **164.04 us** |

The final sampling stage is largely decoupled from vocabulary size
because only the selected 1024-element fine block is reloaded and
scanned.

#### Previous NPU Gumbel-Max comparison

| Batch | Vocab | Previous Gumbel-Max | Categorical | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 151936 | 45366.88 us | 32.86 us | **~1380.6×** |
| 64 | 151936 | 90728.34 us | 164.04 us | **~553.1×** |

The main gain comes from eliminating vocabulary-wide random-number
generation and the two logarithm operations required by the Gumbel
transform.

A representative model workload also showed the sampling cost dropping
from approximately `80324.612 us` to `155.53 us` on average, reducing
its time ratio from `43.689%` to `0.13%` in that workload.

---

### Comparison with V1 `random_sample`

V1 `random_sample` uses exponential-race sampling:

```python
q = empty_exponential_noise_like(probs, use_fp64_gumbel)
q.exponential_()
scores = probs.div_(q)
return scores.argmax(dim=-1)
```

This is also distribution-equivalent to categorical sampling.

For the V1 comparison, `probs` is precomputed so that only the V1
`random_sample` core is profiled. Therefore the V1 numbers below **do
not include softmax or other logits-to-probability preprocessing**,
which intentionally makes the V1 baseline more favorable.

On Ascend A2/A3, `Tensor.exponential_()` is lowered into a sequence
similar to:

```text
Uniform RNG
  -> Neg
  -> Add
  -> GreaterEqual
  -> MaskedFill
  -> Log
  -> Mul
  -> RealDiv
  -> ArgMax
  -> optional Cast
```

The current targeted `msprof op` run captured the exponential transform,
division, `argmax`, and cast stages, but did not expose the underlying
Uniform RNG kernel through the selected kernel-name path. Therefore the
V1 values below are reported as **conservative captured lower bounds**:
the actual V1 `random_sample` device cost is no lower than these values.

#### V1 core — batch growth at `V=151936`

| Batch | Vocab | V1 captured lower bound |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 151936 | **58.80 us** |
| 16 | 151936 | **117.82 us** |
| 32 | 151936 | **176.14 us** |
| 64 | 151936 | **315.52 us** |
| 128 | 151936 | **660.70 us** |
| 256 | 151936 | **1635.60 us** |
| 512 | 151936 | **3755.52 us** |

Additional reviewer-oriented V1 anchors:

| Batch | Vocab | V1 captured lower bound |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 32000 | **48.74 us** |
| 64 | 32000 | **95.32 us** |

#### V1 core — vocabulary growth at `B=64`

| Batch | Vocab | V1 captured lower bound |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 32768 | **94.42 us** |
| 64 | 65536 | **157.58 us** |
| 64 | 131072 | **277.28 us** |
| 64 | 151936 | **315.52 us** |

Using the conservative V1 lower bound above, the long-vocabulary
categorical results are already lower:

| Batch | Vocab | V1 captured lower bound | Categorical | Categorical
speedup vs V1 lower bound |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 151936 | 58.80 us | 32.86 us | **1.79×** |
| 16 | 151936 | 117.82 us | 58.54 us | **2.01×** |
| 32 | 151936 | 176.14 us | 87.68 us | **2.01×** |
| 64 | 151936 | 315.52 us | 164.04 us | **1.92×** |
| 128 | 151936 | 660.70 us | 315.54 us | **2.09×** |
| 256 | 151936 | 1635.60 us | 599.00 us | **2.73×** |
| 512 | 151936 | 3755.52 us | 1163.42 us | **3.23×** |

At `B=64`, the same trend is visible as vocabulary size grows:

| Vocab | V1 captured lower bound | Categorical | Categorical speedup vs
V1 lower bound |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32768 | 94.42 us | 76.18 us | **1.24×** |
| 65536 | 157.58 us | 97.72 us | **1.61×** |
| 131072 | 277.28 us | 144.60 us | **1.92×** |
| 151936 | 315.52 us | 164.04 us | **1.92×** |

The gap grows with larger `B × V` because V1 exponential-race sampling
still performs elementwise work over the full probability tensor, while
the categorical implementation generates only one random value per row
and restricts the final token search to one 1024-element fine block.

---

### Accuracy / probability-distribution validation

The optimized implementation changes the random-number consumption
pattern, so exact sampled token sequences are not expected to match the
previous Gumbel-Max implementation for the same `seed` and `pos`.

The correctness requirement is instead:

> the empirical sampling distribution must match the categorical
distribution defined by the input logits and temperature.

The operator test includes a long-vocabulary business-shape distribution
check:

```text
B = 64
V = 151936
trials = 256
total samples = 16384
```

The finite-probability support spans coarse-block, fine-block, and tail
boundaries:

```text
[7, 1023, 1024, 8191, 8192, 65535, 131071, V - 1]
```

with support logits:

```text
[-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]
```

The empirical probabilities are compared against `torch.softmax` and
must satisfy:

```text
max absolute probability error <= 0.02
total variation distance       <= 0.04
```

This directly exercises:

- the `1024` fine-block boundary,
- the `8192` coarse-block boundary,
- long-vocabulary indexing,
- vocabulary tail handling,
- hierarchical probability-mass reconstruction.

An additional equal-mass random-sampling sanity case verifies that
samples stay within the expected support and that all supported tokens
are reached.

---

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, in sampling sequence behavior.

There is no new public sampling API, and the target probability
distribution is unchanged. However, the internal random-sampling
algorithm changes from Gumbel-Max to direct categorical sampling.

Because the two algorithms consume random numbers differently, the exact
sampled token sequence for the same `seed` and `pos` is **not guaranteed
to match** the previous implementation.

The following properties are preserved:

- greedy results for `temperature == 0`,
- categorical probability distribution for random sampling,
- deterministic replay within the new implementation for identical
inputs,
- request-level temperature / seed behavior,
- raw-logits cache semantics,
- draft-vs-target RNG separation.

---

### How was this patch tested?

Added/updated operator and patch tests:

```text
tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_categorical_sample.py
tests/ut/patch/worker/test_patch_v2_gumbel.py
```

The categorical operator tests cover:

- FP32 / FP16 / BF16 greedy sampling.
- Exact greedy `argmax` behavior for `temperature=0`.
- Mixed greedy and random rows.
- `1024` fine-block boundaries.
- `8192` coarse-block boundaries.
- Non-aligned vocabulary tail at `V=151936`.
- Deterministic replay with identical `seed` and `pos`.
- Target and drafting RNG paths.
- `apply_temperature=True/False` equivalence against pre-scaled logits.
- Raw `logits_cache` semantics.
- Scalar and per-token `logits_cache_col`.
- CUDAGraph padding request mapping (`-1`) without invalid cache writes.
- Shared request mapping.
- Cache-write invariance of sampled output.
- Equal-mass random-distribution sanity.
- `B64 / V151936` empirical probability-distribution validation against
`torch.softmax`.
- Unsupported `use_fp64=True` behavior.

The patch test additionally checks that modules imported before the
Ascend patch are rebound to `categorical_sample`, including
sampler/speculator consumers.

Example operator-test command:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_categorical_sample.py
```

Performance validation uses explicit target-kernel `msprof op` profiling
rather than Python synchronized wall time.

[Performance][Ops] Reduce A5 MLA prolog v3 template combinations (#16516)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

A5 image builds have encountered compiler OOM while building
`mla_prolog_v3`. This applies the A5 non-quantized/MXFP8 scope from
#13844 to main and removes additional selections that the current Host
tiling cannot produce.

- Keep Q0 (BF16), Q7 and Q8 (MXFP8), with matching Query/KV quantization
and PA_BSND for MXFP8.
- Prune unsupported quantization dispatches and unreachable CV/cache
combinations, MXFP8 `DEQUANT=0`, and empty-query `ROPE=0` selections.
- Keep non-quantized cache layouts, both RoPE modes, empty-input
handling, and MXFP8 SplitM.

[BugFix][Model] Fix DeepSeek V4 load-format=dummy profile run failures (#16485)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes two failures when serving DeepSeek V4 with
--load-format=dummy (profile run):

1. Hash MoE routing table (tid2eid) now uses torch.rand(...).topk(...)
instead of a torch.zeros/torch.randint-style initialization. topk over
random scores guarantees each token's top-k expert ids are unique within

load paths diverged:
- load-format=auto:

complete the 2D→3D conversion:

[BugFix][Worker] Scope sleep-mode kv_cache tag to allocate_kv_cache (#16096)

What this PR does / why we need it?
Align with vLLM #53508 / #53343 by passing the kv_cache memory pool into
initialize_kv_cache and entering it only around backing cache
allocation. Persistent metadata stays resident across sleep/wake, so the
post_kv_cache_wake_up reconstruction hook is no longer invoked.

Previously NPUWorker.initialize_from_config() entered the discardable
kv_cache pool around the entire initialize_kv_cache() call. Persistent
runtime tensors created in that scope (attention builders, block tables,
connector state, graph-safe constants) inherited the kv_cache tag and
were discarded on sleep while keeping the same virtual address.

This PR:

Passes kv_cache_allocation_context into MRV1, MRV2, 310P, and Xlite
runners
Enters the pool only around backing cache allocation
(_allocate_kv_cache_tensors / _allocate_kv_cache)
Keeps reshape, sharing, bind, and other setup outside the pool
Stops calling post_kv_cache_wake_up() after KV wake-up, matching
upstream: metadata is now resident, so reconstructing it would replace
graph-captured storage
Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
No. The public sleep/wake API is unchanged. Sleep/wake becomes more
correct for persistent non-KV tensors.

[Revert] Revert "[Performance][Spec Decode] Avoid cloning unused raw target logits" (#16211) (#16678)

Revert of PR #16211 (merged onto `main`).

Original PR: #16211
Original author: @zzy-6666
Merge commit: `0526083dd4aae02a02afeb0de680c119d8e5e732`

---
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR avoids an unnecessary FP32 target-logits clone in the vLLM
Ascend
speculative decoding path.

`AscendRejectionSampler.forward()` preserves the original target logits
before applying logits processors because these processors may modify
the
tensor in place. However, this copy is unnecessary when raw logprobs are
not
requested and Ascend entropy verification is disabled.

Inspired by upstream vLLM PR

[https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53489](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53489),
this change makes the clone conditional while accounting for the
Ascend-specific entropy verification path.

vLLM Ascend passes the original logits to `rejection_sample()` through
`ori_target_logits`. Therefore, the clone is preserved when:

- raw logprobs are requested; or
- Ascend entropy verification is enabled, regardless of the logprobs
mode.

Otherwise, the redundant full-vocabulary tensor copy is skipped.
`max_num_logprobs=0` continues to be treated as a logprobs request, and
processed-logprobs behavior remains unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce *any* user-facing change?

No.

This is an internal performance optimization. The API, generated
results,
and configuration behavior remain unchanged. Original logits are still
preserved whenever they are required for raw logprobs or Ascend entropy
verification.

### How was this patch tested?

The clone path was instrumented and manually verified on 4 × Ascend 910B
with TP=4 before and after the change:

| Entropy verification | Logprobs requested | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disabled | No | Clone executed | Clone skipped |
| Disabled | Yes | Clone executed | Clone executed |
| Enabled | No | Clone executed | Clone executed |
| Enabled | Yes | Clone executed | Clone executed |

A parameterized regression test,
`test_forward_clones_raw_target_logits_only_when_needed`, was also added
to
`tests/ut/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py`. It covers:

- raw-logprobs mode with `max_num_logprobs=None`, `0`, and a positive
value;
- processed-logprobs mode;
- entropy verification in both logprobs modes.

The test uses an in-place logits processor and verifies that processed
logits
are updated while the original logits remain unchanged whenever
required.
In particular, it ensures that entropy verification preserves the
original
logits independently of `is_processed_logprobs_mode`.

Local checks:

- `ruff check`: PASS
- `ruff format --check`: PASS
- Python syntax compilation: PASS
- `git diff --check`: PASS

The regression test passed in the PR CPU UT environment.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add Ascend 950 (A5) support for the existing AddRmsNormBias operator,
with upstream-derived FullLoad and SplitD implementations. Optional beta
is added to the FP32 normalized output before the final output cast.

Wire the implementation through the A5 build list, `ascend950` OpDef
configuration, Host tiling and APT entry. The ordinary `AscendRMSNorm`
residual path lazily imports the existing extension, calls
`enable_custom_op()`, and directly invokes
`torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_add_rms_norm_bias`. Its return value is not
used as a gate. `AscendGemmaRMSNorm` retains its pre-PR implementation,
including its original custom-op gate and native fallback. The generic
capability gate is unchanged; no separate A5 availability helper or new
DeviceOperator method is introduced.

Keep the no-beta tiling when beta is present: FullLoad replaces one
residual-output buffer with a single beta vector; SplitD replaces one
gamma buffer with a single beta tile. Both inputs remain
double-buffered. Output vector functions remain specialized for beta
presence, so the no-beta specialization contains no beta loads or
additions. Both optional-beta cases remain supported.

execution failures propagate instead of falling back to native

returns false, including when batch-invariant mode is enabled; this PR

registration: `register_ascend_customop()` selects `AscendRMSNorm310`
and `AscendGemmaRMSNorm310`. These classes override `forward_oot`, so
their normal registered path does not enter the ordinary-class

[Test] System-level HTTP tests for load_balance_proxy_server + decode error fix (#15271)

## Description

This PR combines:
1. The decode error forwarding fix (issue #12166, previously in #12168)
— decode 4xx/5xx/connection errors are returned with the real HTTP
status code instead of an empty 200.
2. A new **system-level test file**
(`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_load_balance_proxy_server.py`) that verifies
the proxy's HTTP behavior.

## Why system-level tests (not unit tests)?

Unit tests that import/call internal proxy functions break when the
proxy is refactored (function rename, class extraction, etc.).
System-level tests only check **HTTP input → output** (status code +
body), which is the proxy's stable external contract. They survive any
internal refactoring.

## Test approach

- **Self-contained**: the test file includes a mock ASGI backend
(prefill + decode) with a scriptable response queue, started as
subprocesses via `__main__`.
- **Real proxy**: the actual `load_balance_proxy_server_example.py` runs
as a subprocess, pointing at the mock backends.
- **Real client**: `httpx` sends real HTTP requests and asserts status +
body.
- **No internal imports**: the test never imports or calls proxy
internals.

## Coverage (11 scenarios)

| Scenario | Mock decode returns | Expected proxy output |
|---|---|---|
| Normal non-stream | 200 stream + content | 200 + content |
| Normal stream | 200 stream + SSE + [DONE] | 200 + SSE + [DONE] |
| Over-limit 4xx non-stream | 400 `{"error":{...}}` | 400 + error body |
| Over-limit 4xx stream | 400 `{"error":{...}}` | 400 + error body |

| /v1/models | — | 200 |
| /healthcheck | — | 200 |

|

[BugFix] Fix EPLB Tensor List address resolution for weight_assist_matrix in grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 (#16507)

### What this PR does / why we need it

**Symptom**
When running quant MoE models with EPLB (Expert Parallelism Load
Balancing) enabled, severe accuracy degradation or logits divergence
occurs during expert switching. Disabling EPLB resolves the issue.

**Root Cause**
Under EPLB in Model Runner V2, W4A8 expert parameters and auxiliary
matrices (such as `weight_assist_matrix` / `w13_scale_bias`) are split
into individual Tensor List entries via `clone()`, resulting in
non-contiguous memory allocations.

In
`csrc/gmm/grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2/op_kernel/grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2_a8w4_msd_post.h`,
the auxiliary matrix offset calculation in `UpdateAuxiliaryMatrix()`
mistakenly treated single contiguous tensors and Tensor Lists using the
same logic (calculating offsets via flat indexing: `expert_id *
tokenLen`).

When expert switching occurred under EPLB, this led to incorrect memory
address access (reading out-of-bounds or misaligned auxiliary data).
Corrupted scale-bias values were then applied during GMM1
post-processing, propagating through MoE outputs and diverging logits.

**Fix**
Refactored `UpdateAuxiliaryMatrix()` to use the existing dedicated
branching helper function to check whether the input is a Tensor List or
a contiguous tensor. For Tensor Lists, address resolution now correctly
routes through `PreLoadAuxiliaryMatrix(vecConfig)` and
`GetTensorAddr()`.

[Performance] skip per-layer indexer cache for GLM-5.1 IndexCache S layers (#14783)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.1 IndexCache retains an `Indexer` module on static S layers for
weight loading, although those layers reuse another layer's top-k
indices. They previously allocated and wrote an indexer KV cache whose
keys were never consumed.

`runtime_has_indexer` distinguishes the weight-loading module from
runtime cache ownership. Static S layers skip indexer preprocessing,
cache writes and cache allocation in both model runner versions.

normalization, including removal of an empty RoPE view. Regression
coverage checks this together with native/fused preprocessing,

Fixes #15866

commits.message: [Feature] dspark: always replicate the Markov head via ReplicatedGroup (#16345) ### What this PR does / why we need it? The DSpark Markov head (`markov_w1` VocabParallelEmbedding + `markov_w2` ParallelLMHead) serves the draft-decoding causal-correction loop, which runs serially per draft position. Under TP sharding every step pays a TP all-reduce (w1) and all-gather (w2), and these collectives are latency-bound: measured on a TP16 Kimi-K3 DSpark deployment, each costs ~240 us regardless of payload, which dominates the markov loop. This PR replicates the Markov head on every rank instead of sharding it: any `AscendVocabParallelEmbedding` whose prefix contains "markov" is routed to a `ReplicatedGroup` — a pure world_size=1 stand-in (no `hcclCommInitRootInfoConfig`) — so each rank holds the full V x r / r x V table (~150 MB extra HBM per rank) and the per-step collectives disappear. This matches upstream vLLM, where the markov head is replicated unconditionally (vllm#49731; deepseek_v4_dspark in #15496 likewise replicates it), so **no new config option is introduced**: the prefix routing itself is the switch, and it is checked before the lmhead prefix match because "markov_head" contains "head". - before - after ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No new config or API. For DSpark models under TP > 1, the Markov head is now replicated on every rank instead of TP-sharded, matching upstream vLLM behavior: draft outputs are numerically equivalent (any difference is limited to floating-point reduction order), while the per-draft-step TP collectives are removed at the cost of ~150 MB extra HBM per rank. ### How was this patch tested?
